basics.name: Anton Dziatkovskii
basics.label: Developer activation for frontier platforms · founder, Palo Alto AI Research Lab (an independent lab)
basics.summary: I've done developer activation for a frontier platform before — when smart contracts were where LLM agents are now. Classically trained in CS security (MEPhI), 10+ years venture founder (since 2015; in crypto since 2015 — supported early Ethereum and Cardano fundraising efforts in Japan), author of two preprints on multi-agent stability. A superconnector with a builder's toolkit: a decade-deep network of founders, builders, engineers and investors (10,000+ founder calls, 2,000+ institutional-investor calls) — and I automate my own connector work end-to-end, from a self-built CRM to today's AI-agent fleet. Today I run a production multi-machine Claude fleet in public — and write the operating manual as I go. Built with Claude as implementation collaborator; I own problem framing, architecture, evaluation, product decisions and final QA. Based between Palo Alto, CA — the heart of Silicon Valley — and Sintra, PT. US O-1 visa active and EU citizen (Polish passport): authorized to work in the US and anywhere in the EU immediately, no visa sponsorship required.

work.name: Palo Alto AI Research Lab
work.summary: Founded in 2023 in Palo Alto, CA; grew a community of 500+ AI practitioners, including Stanford researchers and big-tech engineers. Production multi-machine Claude fleet run in public: claw-consensus (reproducible multi-machine agent consensus, offline demo, published evals, FAILURE-MODES.md), verbatim-citation-gate (zero-token gate + burden-of-proof judge that catches fabricated RAG citations, MIT), agent-control-plane-casebook (reproducible control-plane failures from the production fleet — each case ships a deterministic repro, a runnable red test and an upstream bug report), the operating manual written day by day (相棒 AIBŌ · The Partner).
highlights: Run an evidence-first reliability program across the AI-agent open-source ecosystem: reproducible cross-project probes, mutation-tested reviews of other people's pull requests, and bug reports that arrive with a deterministic reproduction and a regression test demonstrated failing on the unfixed code

Review accepted by the author, not merely posted — google/adk-python#6957, an OAuth2 client secret leaking over three endpoints: the mutation matrix showed which of the project's own tests stayed green, and the author adopted all three findings within six hours (“genuinely one of the most useful reviews I've gotten on this PR”)

Failure classes driven to an upstream fix: google/adk-python#6887 (session ids normalised on write but not on read) fixed from the report; #6941, filed with a measured root cause, was labelled core, assigned to a maintainer and answered by two third-party pull requests
Credited in a third-party release 40 hours after the report — headroom v2.0.8: “reported by @tonydzi”

Scope of the program since Jul 2026 (verified 2026-09-04): contributions merged into 14 third-party engineering projects — Model Context Protocol Go SDK, UK AISI inspect_ai, QwenLM/qwen-code, google-gemini/cookbook, fastmcp, agno, pydantic/logfire, deepset-ai/haystack-integrations, zilliztech/memsearch — plus 52 issues filed with reproductions

The program runs unattended: 13 daily autonomous lanes on the fleet (code review, live-install documentation QA, issue-first bug reports, thread watch), with human approval gates on anything irreversible

work.name: Platinum Software Development Company / Platinum VC & Incubator
work.summary: Co-founded and ran a startup incubator + software house in APAC since 2015 (11 years), alongside Japanese partner Tetsuji Nagata (Grand Corp; 12 years at Bloomberg before that). The job a partner at 500 Startups or Plug and Play does — deal flow, cohorts, founder coaching, advisor matching, fundraising — done hands-on at a boutique incubator, with rare depth in Silicon Valley and even the Japanese and Korean startup communities. Portfolio ~70% crypto / 30% other, AI startups included.
highlights: Superconnector as a system: founders, builders, engineers and investors matched daily — and every repeatable connector motion (enrichment, matching, follow-up) automated, first with a self-built CRM, today with AI agents
In fundraising since 2017: $35M fund under management, syndicate of 250 VCs/angels; helped portfolio startups raise end-to-end — deck, investor intros, term negotiation
Built a deal-flow machine: 10,000+ founder calls and 2,000+ institutional-investor calls; qualified, enriched investor base across the US, Japan, Korea, China, Australia and Europe

Wrote my own CRM to run it (roots: 5 years building ERP/CRM on Salesforce and Microsoft Navision at Merlion): social enrichment, parsing at scale, lead-to-call pipelines; up to 30 operators worked in it daily; today it is AI-native
Ran cohorts end-to-end: recruited builders, coached founders, matched advisors; enterprise advisory for subsidiaries of Foxconn and ANA Airlines
Shipped crypto-exchange infrastructure: cryptocurrency backends, market-maker engines, high-frequency trading systems; partnerships with hedge funds, market makers, brokers
Managed a distributed engineering org of 40+ developers across APAC as product owner
In 2018 worked with banks and governments in Myanmar, Cambodia, Thailand and Australia (incl. CB Bank in Myanmar and central-bank stakeholders) on frameworks to launch their first stablecoins
Built Solidity curricula and ran hackathons, cohorts and incubations for Web3 builders — from first workshop to shipped mainnet product
Built custom distributed ledgers for enterprise clients (ANA, Foxconn) before “blockchain” was an industry term

Worked with major blockchain foundations — Ethereum, Avalanche, Cardano, Aptos, Sui, Canton — supplying engineers and deal flow (“engineers are the new oil”); crypto ecosystem building maps directly onto LLM ecosystem building
Portfolio focus: crypto INFRASTRUCTURE, not consumer apps — exchanges, market-maker engines, HFT, blockchains, DeFi, Bitcoin L2 (~70% of portfolio)
